root_cause.text: `hid_bpf_hw_request()` in the HID-BPF path trusted the return value from `dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests()` as a safe byte count and used it in `memcpy()` without bounding it to the caller-provided buffer size, allowing a BPF-controlled oversized length to overflow the buffer in `hid_hw_request`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret > size) ret = size;` immediately before `memcpy(buf, dma_data, ret);`, and the CVE/commit message states the return value from `dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests()` “can be arbitrary big” because it comes from struct_ops with no guarantees it “makes sense.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the returned length to the request size before copying data in `hid_bpf_hw_request()`.
intent_record.what: In `hid_bpf_hw_request()`, a new bounds check was added after the call that sets `ret`: `if (ret > size) ret = size;` before the existing `if (ret > 0) memcpy(buf, dma_data, ret);` copy.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from copying more bytes into `buf` than the caller’s requested `size`, even if the upstream operation reports a larger `ret` value. It avoids an out-of-bounds read from `dma_data` and/or overflow of the destination buffer during `memcpy`.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp the returned length to the request size before copying data in `hid_bpf_hw_request()`.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the described bug by bounding the length returned from dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests() to the caller-provided request size before memcpy(), which prevents the overflow in hid_bpf_hw_request().

candidates.rationale: This copies `ret` bytes into `buf` without first ensuring `ret` is bounded by the caller-provided buffer size. If `dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests()` returns an oversized BPF-controlled length, this `memcpy()` can overflow the destination buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies a length returned from dispatch_hid_bpf_raw_requests() directly into buf without clamping it to the caller-provided request size, enabling an oversized BPF-controlled return value to overflow the destination buffer in hid_bpf_hw_request().
